title: On Acknowledging the mistake to everybody
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：acknowledge　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 acknowledge 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the director ① acknowledged the mistake to everybody in silence, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② acknowledges the mistake to everybody twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ acknowledge the mistake to everybody at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ acknowledged the mistake to everybody before — a line in the poster for August 1980 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Acknowledging the mistake to everybody in silence, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ acknowledge their help in the letter twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Acknowledge their help in the letter at once and never mention it again.

By 1993 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ acknowledges their help in the letter in silence every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ acknowledged the mistake to everybody again when nobody else would.

⑩ To acknowledge the mistake to everybody, my mother said in 1998, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody acknowledges the mistake to everybody twice over again and somebody must acknowledge the mistake to everybody in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 承认（一般过去式 acknowledged the mistake to everybody：1986 年导演头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 承认（一般现在 acknowledges the mistake to everybody：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 承认（不定式 to acknowledge the mistake to everybody：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 承认（过去完成时 had acknowledged the mistake to everybody：1980 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 承认（动名词 acknowledging the mistake to everybody 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 答谢（acknowledge their help in the letter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去答谢信里提一句他们的帮助）
G. v. 答谢（acknowledge their help in the letter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 承认（后段两处：新来的演员照例 acknowledges their help in the letter，而母亲又一次 acknowledged the mistake to everybody）

answers.why: acknowledge 意为“承认”，1986 年导演一言不发地承认向所有人认了那个错，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 acknowledged。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，自那以后导演来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 acknowledges。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯承认向所有人认了那个错”，此处为不定式 to acknowledge the mistake to everybody。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1993 年之前就有人承认过，故用过去完成时 had acknowledged。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，导演说“承认向所有人认了那个错这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 acknowledging the mistake to everybody 作主语。
acknowledge 意为“答谢”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去答谢信里提一句他们的帮助”，should ever 之后用原形 acknowledge their help in the letter。
acknowledge 意为“答谢”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻答谢信里提一句他们的帮助（acknowledge their help in the letter at once），以后再也不要提起。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例答谢信里提一句他们的帮助，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 acknowledges。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地承认向所有人认了那个错，用一般过去式 acknowledged 叙述。
acknowledge 意为“承认”，结尾那句是母亲 1998 年的话：要承认向所有人认了那个错，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 acknowledge 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1986 the director acknowledged the mistake to everybody in silence, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director acknowledges the mistake to everybody twice over whenever the theatre asks.
Acknowledging the mistake to everybody in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever acknowledge their help in the letter twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre acknowledges their help in the letter in silence every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother acknowledged the mistake to everybody again, and the theatre remembered that half.
